overview: Docket (1940) on Japanese radio: a trans-Pacific tribute broadcast for Prince Tokugawa with Grew's role, Japan's shortwave programming, and new restrictions on foreign ships' radios at Yokohama.

people.name: Prince Iyesato Tokugawa
people.role: Late prince honored in a July 5, 1940 radio tribute

people.name: Viscount T. Inouye
people.role: Organizer of the Tokugawa memorial broadcast and contributor of remarks

people.name: Count Kobayashi
people.role: Speaker scheduled to broadcast to the United States

people.name: Boyce
people.role: Sender of despatches from the U.S. Consulate at Yokohama

people.name: Javens
people.role: Sender of reports from Japan or Tokyo on Japanese overseas broadcasting

subfiles.title: List of Papers: Wireless Telephone in Japan
subfiles.about: An archival contents list summarizes 1940 correspondence and reports concerning Japanese domestic and overseas radio broadcasting and wartime radio controls.
subfiles.summary: Docket (1940) covers a Tokugawa memorial broadcast with Grew's remarks and a US rebroadcast, Japan's shortwave programming, and Yokohama harbor radio-equipment restrictions.

interest: Shows 1940 Japan-US radio diplomacy around a Tokugawa memorial broadcast and expanding overseas programming.
